title: Enhancing In Situ TEM Characterization of RRAM Devices via Optimized Chip Carrier Designs
content: Recent advances in specimen holder technology and biasing techniques for transmission electron microscopy (TEM) have significantly enhanced our ability to probe the dynamic behaviour of resistive switching materials [1]. For resistive random-access memory (RRAM) devices, in situ investigations provide critical insights into the formation and dissolution of redox-based conductive filaments within the switching layer.
